objectives: Read and run the String Formatting program
Predict the output before running each part
Change one line and explain the new behaviour

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
```python
# ============================================================
# ALL STRING FORMATTING METHODS
# ============================================================
name = "Veera"
age = 30
pi = 3.14159265

# 1. F-Strings (Python 3.6+) — PREFERRED
print(f"Name: {name}, Age: {age}")
print(f"Pi: {pi:.2f}")                 # 3.14
print(f"{'centered':^20}")             #      centered      
print(f"{1000000:,}")                  # 1,000,000
print(f"{255:#x}")                     # 0xff
print(f"{42:08b}")                     # 00101010
print(f"{0.75:.1%}")                   # 75.0%
print(f"{'hello'!r}")                  # 'hello' (repr)
print(f"{name=}")                      # name='Veera' (debug, 3.8+)
print(f"{2+2=}")                       # 2+2=4

# 2. str.format()
print("Name: {}, Age: {}".format(name, age))
print("Name: {0}, again: {0}".format(name))
print("Name: {n}, Age: {a}".format(n=name, a=age))
print("{:>10}".format("right"))        #      right
print("{:<10}".format("left"))         # left      
print("{:^10}".format("center"))       #   center  
print("{:*^10}".format("hi"))          # ****hi****

# 3. % formatting (old style — know it for reading legacy code)
print("Name: %s, Age: %d" % (name, age))
print("Pi: %.2f" % pi)

# 4. Template strings (safe for user-supplied templates)
from string import Template
t = Template("Hello, $name! You are $age years old.")
print(t.substitute(name="Veera", age=30))
# Safe: t.safe_substitute() won't raise on missing keys

# ============================================================
# FORMAT SPEC MINI-LANGUAGE
# ============================================================
# [[fill]align][sign][z][#][0][width][grouping_option][.precision][type]
#
# Align: < left, > right, ^ center, = pad between sign and digits
# Sign:  + always, - negative only (default), space=space for positive
# #:     Prefix 0x, 0o, 0b for hex/oct/bin
# Type:  d=decimal, f=float, e=scientific, %=percentage,
#        b=binary, x=hex, o=octal, s=string, c=character

print(f"{42:+d}")          # +42
print(f"{-42:+d}")         # -42
print(f"{42: d}")          #  42 (space for positive)
print(f"{1234:_}")         # 1_234 (underscore separator)
print(f"{0.00123:.2e}")    # 1.23e-03 (scientific)

# --- Format datetime ---
from datetime import datetime
now = datetime.now()
print(f"{now:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S}")  # 2026-04-19 10:30:00
print(f"{now:%A, %B %d, %Y}")      # Sunday, April 19, 2026
```

sections.title: class Currency
sections.body:
```python
# --- Custom __format__ ---
class Currency:
    def __init__(self, amount, symbol="$"):
        self.amount = amount
        self.symbol = symbol
    
    def __format__(self, spec):
        if spec == "short":
            return f"{self.symbol}{self.amount:.0f}"
        return f"{self.symbol}{self.amount:,.2f}"

price = Currency(1234567.89)
print(f"{price}")          # $1,234,567.89
print(f"{price:short}")    # $1234568
```
